GBLUP parameter estimation and cross-validation with ASReml-R

Source: R/asr_gblup.R
asr_gblup.Rd

asr_gblup() runs the whole GBLUP workflow for one scenario directly in R, so no input files have to be exported for ASReml:

  1. fits the model to every data set in param: variance components, heritability and, for two-trait models, genetic / phenotypic correlations plus an LRT of rg = 0 (idh(trait) vs the full genetic structure, boundary = FALSE);

  2. refits the model to every training set in cv, with the variance components handled as set by cv_vc;

  3. predicts GEBVs of the validation individuals (all of them: they have no own record, so a low reliability is expected and not filtered by default) and returns per fold the predictive ability pa = r(y, GEBV), the accuracy pa / sqrt(h2) (h2 from the full data, Dekkers 2007) and the slope b(y ~ GEBV);

  4. summarises them over folds (n, mean, sd, se), returns the GEBVs of all individuals from the full-data fit with their reliability (flag reliable = rel >= min_rel) and, optionally, writes everything to one Excel workbook.

Long runs are safe: every error, non-convergence, boundary estimate and invalid LRT is recorded in $log (with time, stage and label) instead of stopping the loop; fits that do not converge are first continued with update() (max_update), and are then skipped (nonconv = "skip") or kept. A progress line per fit shows status, iterations, time and the estimated time left.

h2, rg and rp are built from the names of the variance components, not from fixed V positions, so they stay correct when random effects are added (random = ~ ide(id) + litter) or covariance structures change (us, idh/diag, corh, corgh): h2 = Va / (all variances of the trait), rg = Cov_a / sqrt(Va1 Va2) (the correlation itself for corh/corgh), rp = sum of all covariances / sqrt(Vp1 Vp2). The vc_index table shows which V each component is and param$formulas the formulas used. V numbers follow fit$vparameters, the order vpredict() uses. Components fixed at the boundary (bound B) are reported with a warning and in param$boundary. fa() / rr() terms and models with several genetic terms (e.g. maternal str() models) need your own formulas in vpredict.

Single-trait or two-trait models are chosen from the nested data: a value column gives a single-trait model, value1 + value2 a two-trait model (layout of mintyr::w2l_nest() / mintyr::c2p_nest()).

asr_gblup(
  param,
  cv = NULL,
  ginv,
  fixed = ~1,
  random = NULL,
  id = "id",
  traits = NULL,
  genetic_cov = "us",
  random_cov = "us",
  residual_cov = "us",
  cv_vc = c("fixed", "warm", "estimate"),
  vpredict = NULL,
  inbreeding = NULL,
  cv_min_rel = -Inf,
  min_rel = 0.05,
  min_n = 10L,
  neg_to_na = FALSE,
  test_rg = TRUE,
  test_rp = FALSE,
  rp = TRUE,
  na_x = c("include", "fail", "omit"),
  dense = "auto",
  maxit = 100L,
  workspace = "30Gb",
  max_update = 2L,
  nonconv = c("skip", "keep"),
  asreml_args = list(),
  asreml_trace = FALSE,
  on_error = c("warn", "stop"),
  keep_pred = TRUE,
  keep_gebv = TRUE,
  path = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

param

Nested table used for parameter estimation, with a list-column data (e.g. cv_scenarios(...)$st_sp$param).

cv

Cross-validation table with list-columns train and validate (e.g. cv_scenarios(...)$st_sp$cv or the output of mintyr::nest_cv()). NULL (default): genetic parameters only, no cross-validation - e.g. for every group of mintyr::w2l_nest() or every trait pair of mintyr::c2p_nest(). Each row is matched to the row of param that shares its outer columns.

ginv

Inverse relationship matrix as used by vm(): A^-1 for pedigree BLUP (ainverse(ped)), G^-1 for GBLUP (G.inverse(G, sparseform = TRUE)$Ginv.sparse) or H^-1 for single-step GBLUP (H.inverse(...)). It must carry attr(, "INVERSE") = TRUE, otherwise vm() takes it as the relationship matrix itself (a warning is given). With ainverse(), F is taken from its inbreeding attribute when inbreeding is NULL.

fixed

One-sided formula of fixed effects, e.g. ~ hhys. For two-trait models every term is nested in trait (trait + trait:hhys).

random

Optional one-sided formula of further random effects, e.g. ~ ide(id) (permanent environment, repeated records), ~ litter + pen, ~ vm(dam, ginv) + ide(dam) (maternal genetic and permanent maternal environment), ~ vm(id, ginv):herd (genotype x herd interaction). In two-trait models each term gets the structure random_cov. Each term is also reported as a proportion of the phenotypic variance (prop_<term>), with rep (repeatability) for ide(<id>) and rB_<X> (type-B genetic correlation) for vm(<id>, ginv):X.

id

Name of the individual ID column in the nested data.

traits

Optional response column(s), one or two, when the nested data do not use value / value1 + value2, e.g. c("bfs", "nls") for one trait recorded in two herds (cv_scenarios(...)$mt_bt).

genetic_cov, random_cov, residual_cov

Two-trait models: variance structure across traits for the genomic term, the extra random terms and the residual: "us", "idh", "diag", "corv", "corh" or "corgh" (residual: "us", "idh", "diag").

cv_vc

How the variance components are handled in each fold: "fixed" (default, fast): fixed at the full-data estimates (Constraint = "F", maxit = 1; slight information leakage because validation records were used to estimate them); "warm": re-estimated from the training set, starting from the full-data values; "estimate": re-estimated from the training set from default start values (no leakage, slowest).

vpredict

Optional named list of extra vpredict() formulas, e.g. list(rep = rep ~ (V1 + V2) / (V1 + V2 + V3)). Check the V numbers in the vc_index table of a first run: they depend on the model.

inbreeding

Inbreeding coefficients: a data.frame whose first column is the ID and second column F, or a named numeric vector. NULL uses F = 0. For GBLUP, F = diag(G) - 1 is common.

cv_min_rel

Reliability filter for the validation individuals in cross-validation. Default -Inf: none. Validation individuals have no own record, so low reliabilities are expected; a filter keeps only the best-connected individuals, biases PA and shrinks the sample.

min_rel

Reliability threshold for the final GEBVs of the full-data fit ($gebv): sets reliable = rel >= min_rel; no rows are dropped.

min_n

Minimum number of validation individuals with a GEBV and a record for PA, accuracy and slope of a fold; fewer gives NA (n still shows the number). With a low h2 the reliability filter can leave only a handful of individuals, whose PA and slope are noise.

neg_to_na

Set negative PA / accuracy / slope to NA before the summary. Default FALSE: dropping negative values biases the mean upwards; TRUE reproduces the original scripts.

test_rg

Two-trait models only: LRT of rg = 0 (idh(trait) genetic structure, other structures unchanged, boundary = FALSE). If both models end up with the same number of free parameters (df = 0, e.g. a restrained covariance), rg_p is NA with a warning.

test_rp

Two-trait models only: LRT of all covariances = 0 (idh for the genetic, extra random and residual terms; df = number of covariance / correlation parameters). This tests whether the traits are correlated at all, not rp = 0 as such.

rp

Compute the phenotypic correlation. Set FALSE when no individual has records for both traits (e.g. one trait in two herds): the residual covariance is then not estimable and rp is not meaningful.

na_x

na.method(x = ): "include" (default, as in the original scripts) treats missing covariates / factor levels as 0 in the design matrix - centre numeric covariates first; ASReml's own default is "fail".

dense

Put the relationship term in dense. "auto" (default): yes for a (nearly) full inverse such as G^-1 or H^-1, no for a sparse one such as A^-1 from ainverse(), where dense would cost much memory.

maxit, workspace

Passed to asreml() (maxit is 1 for cv_vc = "fixed"). ASReml's own defaults are 13 and "128mb"; two-trait GBLUP usually needs more.

max_update

Number of update() calls (continue iterating from the current estimates) on a fit that has not converged; recorded in param$updates and accuracy$cv_updates.

nonconv

What to do with a fit that has still not converged: "skip" (default) - a parameter fit is reported with status = "not_converged" and its CV rows are skipped, a CV fit gives NA for that fold; "keep" - use it anyway. Always recorded in $log.

asreml_args

Named list of further asreml() arguments, e.g. list(ai.sing = TRUE).

asreml_trace

Show ASReml's iteration monitor. Default FALSE: the progress lines of mintyrasr are shown instead.

on_error

"warn" (default): a failing fit is recorded in $log, gives NA results and the loop continues (one warning at the end). "stop": stop at the first failure.

keep_pred

Return the validation predictions (pred).

keep_gebv

Return the GEBVs of all individuals from the full-data fits (gebv: gebv, pev, inb (F), rel, reliable).

path

Optional .xlsx file to write the results to.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

A list of class asr_gblup:

  • varcomp, vc_index: variance components and which V is which;

  • param: h2, rg, rp (+ SE), formulas, status, converge, updates, iterations, loglik, boundary, tests;

  • accuracy: one row per fold and trait: status, n, pa, accuracy, slope, va, h2_full, cv_converge, cv_updates, cv_iter (length of the iteration history: about the number of REML iterations, 2 for fixed variances);

  • summary: n, mean, sd, se over the folds with status == "ok";

  • pred (if keep_pred): validation individuals;

  • gebv (if keep_gebv): all individuals of the full-data fits;

  • log: every error, non-convergence, boundary estimate and invalid LRT.

A status other than "ok" (failed, not_converged, param_failed, param_not_converged, no_start_values) marks rows left out of summary. Fitted model objects are not kept, which keeps memory use low.

See also

asr_scenarios() to run several scenarios from mintyr::cv_scenarios() in one call.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(asreml)
sc <- mintyr::cv_scenarios(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf"), id = "id",
                           group = "test_herd", v = 5, repeats = 5,
                           seed = 2026, out_type = "df")
res <- asr_gblup(sc$st_sp$param, sc$st_sp$cv, ginv = ginv,
                 fixed = ~ hhys, inbreeding = inbreeding,
                 path = "st_sp_ginv.xlsx")
res$vc_index   # which V is which component
res$summary
} # }
